projectDescription: A pet-grooming appointment assistant that gathers booking details, checks deterministic fake availability, and confirms or adjusts appointments through a text-first conversation.

services.name: PawPal Assistant API
services.description: A deterministic Python conversation brain and API for grooming appointment intake, validation, fake availability checks, and booking-state responses.

services.name: PawPal Web App
services.description: A React text-first assistant interface showing the conversation and the assistant's current decision state.

questions.question: Which language should power the PawPal Assistant API?
questions.rationale: The requested deterministic backend brain must be implemented in Python.

options.label: Python
options.description: Build the API and deterministic conversation logic in Python.

options.label: C# (.NET)
options.description: Build the API and conversation logic with .NET.

options.label: JavaScript
options.description: Build the API with JavaScript on Node.js.

options.label: TypeScript
options.description: Build the API with TypeScript on Node.js.

questions.question: Which Python framework should the PawPal Assistant API use?
questions.rationale: FastAPI provides a lightweight, typed HTTP API suitable for this focused assistant.

options.label: FastAPI
options.description: A lightweight Python framework with typed request and response models.

options.label: Flask
options.description: A minimal Python web framework with a small core.

questions.question: What should the PawPal Assistant API do?
questions.recommendedChoice: Implement deterministic grooming appointment intake and conversational state; validate pet/service/date/time details; use fake availability only; handle corrections and unavailable slots; return visible decision state; include automated tests. Do not use an LLM for decisions.
questions.answer: Implement deterministic grooming appointment intake and conversational state; validate pet/service/date/time details; use fake availability only; handle corrections and unavailable slots; return visible decision state; include automated tests. Do not use an LLM for decisions.
questions.rationale: These requirements are explicit in the accepted PawPal scope and the repository task.

questions.question: Which language should the PawPal web app use?

questions.question: Which frontend framework should PawPal use?
questions.rationale: React was explicitly requested for the frontend.

questions.question: What should the PawPal web app show and support?
questions.recommendedChoice: Provide a text-first chat interface with a visible conversation transcript and current decision/booking state. Make browser speech recognition and synthesis a stretch goal only after the text interaction works.
questions.answer: Provide a text-first chat interface with a visible conversation transcript and current decision/booking state. Make browser speech recognition and synthesis a stretch goal only after the text interaction works.
questions.rationale: This matches the accepted scope; voice features are explicitly optional and secondary.

questions.question: Which data stores does PawPal need?
questions.rationale: Availability is fake and the accepted scope does not require persistence, file storage, queues, or cache.

options.label: No datastore required

options.description: A relational database for persistent application records.

options.description: Object storage for files and media.

options.label: Azure Queue Storage
options.description: A queue for asynchronous background work.

options.label: Azure Cache for Redis
options.description: A managed cache for low-latency state.
